param.name: providers
param.label: Beacon providers to query
param.help: Each selected provider is queried independently and results are combined, tagged with their origin. One unreachable beacon never fails the job: check the run report output to see what each provider did.

validator.message: No Beacon providers are enabled on this Galaxy instance. An administrator can enable them in the beacon_providers data table (tool-data/beacon_providers.loc).

param.name: granularity
param.label: Level of detail requested
param.help: Beacons are not obliged to honour this: a provider may return less than you ask for, and the run report records what each one actually returned. Record level is required for the frequency and matrix tools.
param.option: Record — full details of each match

param.label: Page size
param.help: Number of records per page. 0 requests everything the beacon is willing to return.

param.label: Accept a random sample of this size (optional)
param.help: Some beacons return a different random subset for any request smaller than the full result, so by default the tool retrieves everything or refuses. Set this to accept a random sample instead; every row is then labelled as a sample, and a repeat run returns different rows.

param.label: Pages to skip
param.help: This counts PAGES, not records — the record offset is (pages skipped × page size). Skipping 2 pages with a page size of 8 starts at record 17.

repeat.name: filters
repeat.title: Filter
repeat.help: Filters scope a query by ontology term, numeric value or local identifier. Multiple filters are combined with AND.

param.name: kind
param.label: Filter type
param.option: Custom term defined by the beacon

param.name: term
param.label: Term (CURIE)
param.help: For example NCIT:C6975 (papillary renal cell carcinoma), HP:0100526, or PMID:22824167. Use the Filtering Terms tool to discover what a provider accepts.

validator.message: Enter a CURIE such as NCIT:C6975

param.name: include_descendant_terms
param.label: Include descendant terms
param.help: On by default, matching the specification: querying a parent term also matches its children.

param.name: field
param.label: Field identifier
param.help: Preferably a CURIE scoping the field, for example PATO:0000011 (age) or EFO:0004847 (age at onset).

param.name: value
param.label: Value
param.help: Use % as a wildcard, e.g. %cancer%. Enter ages in YEARS — they are converted to the ISO 8601 form the API requires (70 becomes P70Y).

param.name: is_age
param.label: This value is an age in years
param.help: Converts your number to an ISO 8601 period before transmission.

param.name: term
param.label: Custom term
param.help: A locally defined identifier, using whatever prefix the beacon documents.

param.name: scope
param.label: Apply this filter to (optional)
param.help: Resolves an ambiguity that otherwise changes your results: a cancer term with no scope can mean 'match cancer biosamples' or 'match individuals with the disease', and the second can pull in germline variants alongside tumour ones.

param.label: Chromosome
param.help: Enter it however you normally write it — 17, chr17 or NC_000017.11 are all accepted and converted to whatever the provider expects.

param.label: Genome assembly
param.help: Used for providers that identify chromosomes by name rather than by RefSeq accession.

param.name: variant_classes
param.label: Variant classes to search
param.help: Each class is queried separately against each beacon, and the run report has a row for every combination — so a beacon that returns nothing tells you why. Not every beacon holds every class.
param.option: Copy number variants — gains, losses, amplifications
SNV / small indel — substitutions and short insertions or deletions

validator.message: Select at least one variant class.

section.name: cnv_terms
section.title: Copy number term (used if Copy number variants is selected)

param.name: mode
param.label: Copy number term
param.help: DEL and DUP are what the Beacon specification itself calls legacy variant types; it prefers the EFO terms.

param.name: expand_hierarchy
param.label: Expand to more specific terms
param.help: Querying 'copy number gain' without expansion can miss amplifications recorded under a more specific term — a false negative you cannot see in the output.
param.option: Automatically — expand unless the beacon does it itself
Never — send the single term only

section.name: small_variant_terms
section.title: SNV / small indel scoping (used if that class is selected)

param.name: reference_bases
param.label: Reference bases
param.help: The bases in the reference sequence, e.g. G. Use N as a wildcard.

param.name: alternate_bases
param.label: Alternate bases
param.help: The bases you are looking for, e.g. A. Use N as a wildcard: ANNT matches ACGT, ACCT and so on.

param.name: aminoacid_change
param.label: Amino acid change
param.help: One-letter format, e.g. V600E.

param.name: term
param.label: Term
param.help: For example SNV, INS or DEL, or any value the beacon accepts.

section.name: sv_terms
section.title: Structural variant scoping (used if that class is selected)

param.name: transport
param.label: Beacon connection
param.help: This tool reads the Beacon v2 API's informational endpoints, which a self-hosted MongoDB database does not have.

param.label: Database host
param.help: Hostname or IP of your self-hosted beacon database.

#if "CNV" in str($variant_classes).split(",") #if str($cnv_terms.variant_type.mode) == "efo" --class-term 'CNV=$cnv_terms.variant_type.term' --expand-hierarchy '$cnv_terms.variant_type.expand_hierarchy' #elif str($cnv_terms.variant_type.mode) != "none" --class-term 'CNV=$cnv_terms.variant_type.term' #end if #end if

#if "SMALL_VARIANT" in str($variant_classes).split(",") #if str($small_variant_terms.reference_bases) --reference-bases '$small_variant_terms.reference_bases' #end if #if str($small_variant_terms.alternate_bases) --alternate-bases '$small_variant_terms.alternate_bases' #end if #if str($small_variant_terms.aminoacid_change) --aminoacid-change '$small_variant_terms.aminoacid_change' #end if #if str($small_variant_terms.variant_type.mode) != "none" --class-term 'SMALL_VARIANT=$small_variant_terms.variant_type.term' #end if #end if
This tool **reads**: it searches beacons and never changes them. To load data into a self-hosted beacon, use **Beacon2 Import**.
This tool **writes**: it loads Beacon JSON into a self-hosted beacon's MongoDB database, and it is the only Beacon2 tool that changes data. To search, use the Beacon2 query tools.

**Outputs**
*Results* — one row per match. Every row carries the beacon it came from, the level of detail that beacon actually returned, and whether the query had to be weakened to run there. Because each row is tagged, filtering on ``beacon_id`` recovers any single-beacon view: you do not need a separate run per provider.
*Run report* — one row for every combination of beacon and variant class, with a status of ``ok``, ``skipped``, ``auth_missing``, ``blocked``, ``unavailable`` or ``error``. Read it first. Two classes across three beacons gives six rows, and each one says what happened. Without it, a beacon returning nothing looks identical to a beacon that was never queried, or to one that does not hold that kind of variant.

**Not every beacon holds every kind of variant**
Whether a beacon can *answer* a query and whether it *holds* that kind of data are different things, and the Beacon protocol has no way to ask about the second. A resource can implement small-variant queries perfectly and hold almost nothing but copy number profiles.
So the tool ships a registry recording, per beacon, which classes it is known to serve, and every result is labelled with the class it belongs to:
* **known to serve it** — queried normally * **not known either way** — queried anyway, and the row is marked unverified. If nothing comes back, the report says so in as many words: that is not evidence the beacon holds none * **declared not to serve it** — skipped, quoting the declaration
Most entries start as *not known either way*, because this genuinely cannot be read from a beacon's own metadata. Fetching a beacon's information endpoint tells you its version, its security level and its schemas, and nothing at all about whether it holds a single copy number variant. As people use the tool, results returned for an unverified class are reported as evidence that the registry can be updated.

**Large indels are classified by what is known about them, not by size**
A 120 base insertion is not a small variant in any ordinary sense, but if the beacon reports the reference and alternate bases then it is *precisely specified by sequence* — we know exactly what was inserted and where. That is the same kind of knowledge as for a single base change, so it is reported as **SNV / small indel**, with the length noted in ``classification_basis``.
It is deliberately not reported as a structural variant. Structural variant analysis counts breakpoints, and a record that gives bases rather than a junction has no breakpoint to count — it would either sit in that bucket contributing nothing, or invite something downstream to invent a breakpoint from the interval ends.
To find large events whatever their class, filter on the ``variant_length`` column in the results table rather than on ``variant_class``. For example, ``variant_length >= 50`` gives every event of that size across all classes.
The same record with *no* reported bases behaves differently, and correctly so: with no sequence and no junction, there is nothing to classify on, so it is reported as a copy number variant if the beacon supplied a copy number term and as ``unclassified`` if it did not.

**When a query cannot be run as asked**
Beacons differ in what they support. Rather than failing, the tool weakens the query where it must and records what it did on every affected row: a bracket query flattened to a range, an EFO term downgraded to DEL/DUP, a filter dropped, or detail capped. Check ``query_degraded`` and ``degradation_notes`` before comparing results between providers.

**Copy number terms**
Users think in DEL and DUP; the wire format prefers EFO terms. Enter either.
====================== =================================== ==== =========== EFO term Meaning VCF SO ====================== =================================== ==== =========== EFO:0030067 copy number loss DEL SO:0001743 EFO:0030068 low-level copy number loss DEL SO:0001743 EFO:0020073 high-level copy number loss DEL SO:0001743 EFO:0030069 complete genomic deletion DEL SO:0001743 EFO:0030070 copy number gain DUP SO:0001742 EFO:0030071 low-level copy number gain DUP SO:0001742 EFO:0030072 high-level copy number gain DUP SO:0001742 EFO:0030073 focal genome amplification DUP SO:0001742 EFO:0030064 regional base ploidy — — ====================== =================================== ==== ===========
Note ``EFO:0020073``: high-level loss uses a ``002`` prefix, breaking the pattern of the others.
**A documented discrepancy.** Two GA4GH sources disagree about this vocabulary. The query-standards component lists eight terms including regional base ploidy but omitting focal amplification; the CNV comparison table lists eight including focal amplification but omitting regional base ploidy. We support all nine. Because regional base ploidy appears only in the first source, it has no VCF or SO mapping, and we leave those cells empty rather than invent them.
**One local decision.** No authority states where focal amplification sits in the hierarchy. We place it beneath high-level gain, because it describes the same copy threshold with an added size constraint. When expansion crosses that edge, the affected rows say so in ``expansion_notes`` — so you can tell a match found through our inference from one found through a published hierarchy.
